title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Guiding Opinions on Fully Leveraging Judicial Functions to Support the Development of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Guiding Opinions on Giving Full Play to the Role of Judicial Functions to Support the Development of Micro, Small, and Medium-sized Enterprises

Fa Fa [2022] No. 2

Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Guiding Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Giving Full Play to the Role of Judicial Functions to Support the Development of Micro, Small, and Medium-sized Enterprises are hereby issued to you for earnest implementation.

January 13, 2022

Guiding Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Giving Full Play to the Role of Judicial Functions to Support the Development of Micro, Small, and Medium-sized Enterprises

Micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) are a vital force for national economic and social development and an important driver of expanding employment, improving people's livelihoods, and promoting entrepreneurship and innovation. Further increasing support for MSMEs and stimulating their vitality and development momentum is of great significance for continuing the work of stabilizing employment, the financial sector, foreign trade, foreign investment, domestic investment, and expectations (the "six stability" work) and ensuring security in employment, basic necessities, market entities, food and energy security, stable industrial and supply chains, and the smooth functioning of society (the "six guarantees" work), stabilizing the macroeconomic landscape, accelerating the formation of a new development pattern, and promoting high-quality development. To fully, accurately, and comprehensively implement the new development philosophy, further leverage the judicial functions of people's courts, and assist the development of MSMEs, the following opinions are hereby proposed.

I. Actively Create a Market Environment of Fair Competition and Honest Operation

1. Protect the survival and development space of MSMEs in accordance with law. Fairly and efficiently adjudicate antitrust and anti-unfair competition cases, and severely punish illegal acts such as forced "choose one of two," below-cost sales, forced tying, blocking and shielding, and click farming and fake reviews. In accordance with law, determine whether operators have abused data, algorithms, technology, capital advantages, or platform rules to exclude or restrict competition, prevent the disorderly expansion of capital, and protect the survival and development space of MSMEs. Strengthen the mechanism for linking judiciary with law enforcement, support antitrust administrative agencies in performing their duties according to law, strengthen communication and coordination, and promote the formation of a joint working force.

2. Serve to deepen the reform of "streamlining administration, delegating power, improving regulation, and upgrading services." Strengthen administrative adjudication, support administrative agencies in rectifying illegal operations and regulating market order. In accordance with law, supervise and promote administrative agencies to conduct supervision strictly within statutory authority and procedures, and protect the autonomy of MSMEs in business operations. Promote the removal of regional segmentation and local protection, and facilitate the implementation of a nationwide unified negative list system for market access. Strengthen the sharing and integration of information related to litigation involving market entities with relevant departments, and provide strong judicial support for building a new type of regulatory mechanism based on credit.

3. Support and protect voluntary transactions among market entities. In adjudicating contract dispute cases, adhere to the principle of voluntariness and the principle of encouraging transactions, accurately determine the statutory grounds for finding contracts void, reasonably assess the validity of contracts arising from various transaction models and structural innovations, fully leverage the initiative of MSMEs, and promote the enhancement of market economic vitality. Promote the spirit of contracts. Where a market entity with a dominant position takes advantage of an MSME being in a state of distress or lacking the ability to judge complex contract content, resulting in the contract being manifestly unfair at the time of formation, and the MSME requests to revoke the contract, support shall be given. Where a market entity with a dominant position uses standard terms to enter into a contract with an MSME, and fails to fulfill the obligation to draw attention to or explain terms having a material bearing on the MSME's interests in accordance with Article 496, Paragraph 2 of the Civil Code, causing the MSME not to notice or understand such terms, and the MSME argues that such terms do not form part of the contract, support shall be given. Where a contract cannot be performed by an MSME directly due to factors such as the epidemic, or if continuing to perform the contract is manifestly unfair to it, the rules on force majeure or change of circumstances shall be applied in accordance with Article 590 or Article 533 of the Civil Code for proper handling.

4. Support and guide market entities to operate honestly and in good faith. In adjudicating contract dispute cases, where a party violates obligations stipulated in a preliminary contract or maliciously negotiates under the pretext of concluding a contract in violation of the principle of good faith, strengthen the application of systems such as liability for breach of preliminary contracts and pre-contractual liability to enhance market entities' awareness of good faith, rules, and responsibility. After determining that a contract is not formed, void, or revoked in accordance with law, reasonably determine the legal liability of both parties based on the specific circumstances, preventing a dishonest party from benefiting from the contract not being formed, being void, or being revoked. Promote the building of litigation integrity, and severely punish illegal acts such as fraudulent litigation and malicious litigation that hinder the normal business development of MSMEs. Strengthen enforcement efforts, and severely crack down on acts of bad faith debtors who evade enforcement by opening multiple bank accounts, engaging in related party transactions, changing legal representatives, or other means.

II. Effectively Strengthen Judicial Protection of Property Rights of MSMEs

5. Protect the lawful rights and interests of MSMEs fairly and impartially. Adhere to the principle of equal rights, equal opportunities, and equal rules for all types of market entities. In litigation proceedings, treat large enterprises and MSMEs equally. Fully consider the actual circumstances of MSMEs, provide them with litigation guidance and clarification according to law, strengthen the collection of evidence ex officio, effectively ascertain the facts of the case, prevent the vulnerable position of some MSMEs in market transactions from being transformed into an unfavorable position in litigation, and strive to achieve the unity of procedural fairness and substantive fairness. Continue to improve the one-stop diversified dispute resolution mechanism, promote online litigation models, strengthen the application of summary procedures and small claims procedures, enhance litigation convenience, and effectively reduce the litigation costs of MSMEs. By reasonably determining the amount of preservation guarantees, introducing preservation liability insurance guarantees, and other means, reduce the preservation costs for MSMEs and ensure the realization of winning creditors' claims. For MSMEs facing severe operational difficulties, provide judicial relief such as reduction or deferral of litigation costs in accordance with law.

6. Strengthen the protection of intellectual property rights of MSMEs. Implement the system of punitive damages for intellectual property infringement, strengthen the protection of key core technologies and original innovation achievements of "specialized, refined, characteristic, and innovative" MSMEs, and support and guide enterprises to enhance their core competitiveness through technological progress and scientific innovation. Where an MSME, in the process of obtaining specific technology through a technology transfer contract or technology licensing contract, is subjected by the other party to unreasonable conditions that restrict technology competition or technological improvement, or is unreasonably required to transfer newly developed technologies or products for free or at a low price, and upon examination it is found that such conditions violate mandatory provisions of the Anti-Monopoly Law or other laws, the relevant clauses or the contract shall in principle be found void. Properly handle the relationship between protecting trade secrets and the reasonable flow of personnel. While safeguarding the legitimate employment and entrepreneurship rights of workers, protect the trade secrets of MSMEs in accordance with law. Sanction dishonest litigation and malicious litigation according to law, and regulate illegal acts that abuse intellectual property rights to hinder the innovation of MSMEs.

7. Resolutely prevent the use of criminal means to intervene in economic disputes involving MSMEs. Strictly implement legal principles such as nulla poena sine lege and presumption of innocence, strictly distinguish between legitimate financing and illegal fundraising by MSMEs, contract disputes and contract fraud, participation in mergers and reorganizations and malicious appropriation of state-owned assets, and resolutely prevent the characterization of economic disputes as criminal offenses and civil liability as criminal liability. Implement the provisions of the Criminal Law and relevant judicial interpretations. Where an MSME illegally or in disguised form absorbs public deposits, mainly for normal production and business activities, and is able to promptly return the absorbed funds, criminal punishment may be exempted; if the circumstances are obviously minor and the harm is not serious, it shall not be treated as a crime.

8. Protect the lawful rights and interests of market entities such as MSMEs in cases involving overlapping civil, administrative, and criminal liabilities. Effectively implement the provisions of Article 187 of the Civil Code. Where a debtor bears civil, administrative, and criminal liabilities due to the same act and its property is insufficient to pay all liabilities, ensure that the civil claims of market entities such as MSMEs are satisfied in priority over fines, criminal fines, confiscation of property, and other administrative or criminal penalties in accordance with law. In the enforcement of the property portion of criminal judgments, where market entities such as MSMEs, as parties not involved in the case, raise objections to the subject matter of enforcement, handle them properly in strict accordance with relevant provisions, and protect their lawful property rights and interests. Unless otherwise provided by law or judicial interpretations, for civil disputes between market entities such as MSMEs and criminal suspects or defendants in criminal cases, if the civil case does not necessarily need to be adjudicated based on the outcome of the criminal case, the civil case shall not be dismissed or stayed on the grounds that the criminal case is under investigation or has not yet been concluded, so as to effectively avoid the impact of the criminal case on market entities such as MSMEs in protecting their lawful rights and interests in a timely manner through civil litigation. In the adjudication of criminal cases where market entities such as MSMEs are defendants, strictly distinguish between illegal gains and lawful property, between property of the enterprise as a legal person and personal property. For property that is indeed unrelated to the case, measures of sealing up, seizing, or freezing shall be promptly lifted.

III. Assist in Alleviating the Difficulty and High Cost of Financing for MSMEs

9. Adjudicate financial loan dispute cases properly and in accordance with law. For claims made by financial institutions in litigation, such as acceleration of loan maturity or unilateral rescission of contracts, based on inclusive MSME loan support policies, support shall not be given. For interest charged by financial institutions, as well as disguised interest collected under the names of consulting fees, guarantee fees, or other charges, the portion exceeding the concessional loan interest rate policy for supporting agriculture and small enterprises shall not be supported.

10. Assist in broadening financing channels for MSMEs. In strict accordance with the provisions of the Civil Code and relevant judicial interpretations, recognize the priority right to satisfaction of security interests over movables such as production equipment, as well as atypical security interests such as retention of title, financial leases, and factoring, and support MSMEs in broadening financing channels according to their actual circumstances. For pledges of warehouse receipts, bills of lading, bills of exchange, accounts receivable, intellectual property rights, and other rights, as well as confirming warehouse transactions, which comply with legal provisions, recognize their validity and support financial institutions in innovating credit products serving MSMEs. Effectively promote supply chain finance to better serve the development of the real economy. For fees generated in supply chain finance transactions, explore the formation of necessity and appropriateness principles based on the type of fee, reasonably limit transaction costs, and effectively reduce the financing costs of MSMEs. Actively share enterprise litigation information with the National SME Financing Comprehensive Credit Service Platform to facilitate precise "profiling" of MSME credit evaluations and increase the availability of loans for enterprises.

11. Regulate the private lending market order in accordance with law. For illegal lending activities such as "relending at high interest rates" and "professional money lending," find them void in accordance with law. Encourage people's courts in various regions to establish a list system for "professional money lenders" based on local conditions. In accordance with law, nullify contract clauses that evade the upper limit of interest rates protected judicially. For disguised high-interest portions exceeding the interest rates stipulated by law and judicial interpretations, support shall not be given. During adjudication or enforcement, if suspicions of illegal fundraising, "loan shark schemes," or collection of illegal debts are discovered, relevant materials shall be promptly transferred to the relevant departments.

IV. Handle Cases of Delayed Payment to MSMEs Efficiently and in Accordance with Law

12. Establish and improve a long-term mechanism for handling cases involving delayed payment to MSMEs. Include cases of delayed payment to MSMEs in the "green channel" for rapid filing, trial, and enforcement of cases involving delayed wages for migrant workers, ensuring that MSMEs where migrant workers are concentrated can promptly recover accounts receivable and timely pay migrant workers' wages. Collaborate closely with supervisory departments for delayed payment to MSMEs to promote coordinated governance. Strengthen the application of the "Peaceful Construction" performance evaluation (the part on comprehensive governance and source governance of enforcement difficulties) in cases where government agencies, public institutions, and large enterprises delay payment to MSMEs. Promote the inclusion of the status of clearing delayed payments to MSMEs in the business environment indicator system. Carry out special enforcement actions for cases of delayed payment to MSMEs, intensify the application of measures such as dishonesty punishment and restrictions on high consumption in accordance with law, and timely realize the winning rights and interests of MSMEs.

13. Effectively prevent relevant market entities from harming the lawful rights and interests of MSMEs. Where government agencies, public institutions, or large enterprises refuse or delay payment to MSMEs on obviously unreasonable grounds such as a change in legal representative or principal responsible person, internal payment procedures, or awaiting completion acceptance and final accounts audit in the absence of contractual provisions, and an MSME files a lawsuit requesting payment, the people's court shall support such a claim. Where government agencies, public institutions, or large enterprises force MSMEs to accept unequal conditions regarding delayed payment, reaching agreements to offset debts with property that are manifestly contrary to market prices, or stipulating obviously unreasonable payment terms or conditions, and an MSME requests to revoke such agreements or terms on grounds of obvious unfairness, the people's court shall support such a claim.

14. Protect the lawful rights and interests of MSMEs and migrant workers in the construction field in accordance with law. Exercise caution in taking preservation or enforcement measures against funds in accounts for supervision of pre-sale proceeds of commercial housing, dedicated accounts for migrant workers' wages, and wage guarantee accounts. Support relevant departments in preventing and responding to the risk of overdue delivery of real estate projects, protect the lawful rights and interests of homebuyers, and ensure the payment of migrant workers' wages. When freezing an account for supervision of pre-sale proceeds of commercial housing, promptly notify the local housing and urban-rural construction department. Unless it is a case where a party applies for enforcement of claims such as progress payments for construction, materials, or equipment arising from the construction of the commercial housing project, before the first registration of ownership of the commercial housing project is completed, no seizure or transfer of funds within the supervised amount in the supervisory account shall be made, nor shall it affect the lawful use of funds in the account in accordance with regulations. Unless otherwise specifically provided by law, the funds in the dedicated account for migrant workers' wages and the wage guarantee account shall not be frozen or transferred for reasons other than paying wages to migrant workers working on the project. For the needs of handling cases, people's courts may take pre-freezing measures against the two types of accounts mentioned above.

V. Effectively Leverage the Judicial Function of Rescuing MSMEs

15. Actively facilitate the parties to reach a settlement agreement in enforcement. During enforcement, where an MSME is unable to repay enforcement debts due to liquidity difficulties, actively guide the parties to reach an enforcement settlement agreement involving debt reduction or deferred payment. Where multiple cases are under the jurisdiction of different people's courts, they may be centrally handled through elevation of jurisdiction or designation of jurisdiction, actively facilitating the parties to reach a "package" agreement for fulfilling debts, thereby creating conditions for alleviating the debt pressure and restoring production and operation of the enterprise in accordance with law.

16. Scientifically identify and protect MSMEs with rescue value in accordance with law. For MSMEs that are unable to pay all debts due to factors such as the epidemic but have rescue value, if creditors file for bankruptcy, actively guide the parties to conduct out-of-court settlement through debt restructuring, asset restructuring, or other means to help the enterprise overcome difficulties. For MSMEs that have entered bankruptcy proceedings but have rescue value, actively guide the enterprise to resolve the debt crisis comprehensively through bankruptcy reorganization, settlement, or other procedures, equitably and orderly satisfy the corresponding claims, and enable the enterprise to achieve rehabilitation.

VI. Minimize the Adverse Impact of Preservation and Enforcement Measures on Market Entities Such as MSMEs

17. Thoroughly review issues of excessive or disorderly sealing up. Carry out special corrective actions to promptly correct issues of excessive or disorderly sealing up in accordance with law. People's courts at all levels shall rely on the 12368 judicial service hotline, enforcement complaints, and other channels for reporting issues to establish a rapid response mechanism for resolving excessive or disorderly sealing up, promptly receiving and quickly addressing issues raised by the parties. Where enforcement personnel are at fault for excessive or disorderly sealing up, pursue accountability strictly and in accordance with law.

18. Exercise caution in taking property preservation measures in accordance with law. When taking preservation measures against market entities such as MSMEs, people's courts shall strictly examine the application in accordance with the standards and procedures prescribed by law. If a preliminary examination finds that the party's claim is manifestly unfounded, the preservation application shall be dismissed in accordance with law. Where a party's preservation application clearly exceeds the scope of the claim, the excessive part of the application shall not be supported. In monetary debt cases, where a market entity such as an MSME that has been subjected to preservation measures provides a guarantee and requests dissolution of the preservation measures, if the guarantee is found to be sufficient and effective upon examination, the request shall be granted by order, and the consent of the preservation applicant shall not be a necessary condition. Strengthen the review of damages cases for erroneous preservation, and severely punish illegal acts of maliciously applying for preservation to hinder the normal business development of market entities such as MSMEs.

19. Flexibly take sealing up and realization measures in accordance with law. When sealing up productive assets such as factory buildings and machinery equipment of market entities such as MSMEs, priority shall be given to adopting "live sealing" measures. Where the interests of creditors can be safeguarded, the entity shall be allowed to continue using such property or to use it for financing. If the overall value of the real property to be sealed clearly exceeds the amount of the claim, sealing measures shall be taken only on the corresponding value portion of the real property. If the real property is sealed up as a whole because it has not been subdivided and registered, the relevant departments shall be promptly coordinated to carry out subdivision registration and lift the sealing on the excessive part. Actively guide the parties to determine the reference price for property disposal through negotiation, inquiry, or other means, effectively saving appraisal costs for the enforced market entities such as MSMEs. Leverage the advantages of high premium rates and low costs of online judicial auctions, and give priority to the application of online judicial auctions for property disposal. For properties such as real property with a large subject matter amount or complex circumstances, where the enforced market entity such as an MSME believes that the reference price determined by entrusted appraisal is too low and applies for self-disposal within a set period, the people's court may permit such disposal if the interests of creditors can be safeguarded.

20. Apply credit punishment and consumption restriction measures accurately and in accordance with law. Strictly distinguish between the application conditions for credit punishment measures and consumption restriction measures. Where a market entity such as an MSME that is subject to enforcement meets only the conditions for consumption restriction but not the conditions for dishonesty, it shall not be included in the list of dishonest persons subject to enforcement. Strictly distinguish between dishonesty and loss of ability to perform. Where a market entity such as an MSME loses the ability to perform due to business failure and does not have illegal circumstances such as evasion or resistance to enforcement as stipulated by law or judicial interpretations, it shall not be included in the list of dishonest persons on the grounds that it has the ability to perform but refuses to do so. Improve the credit restoration mechanism. Where the dishonest information of a market entity such as an MSME meets the statutory conditions for shielding, shielding measures shall be taken promptly. After the dishonest information is shielded, if the entity requests a credit restoration certificate due to needs such as financing or bidding, the people's court may issue relevant supporting materials.
